oewn-03422255-n.learner: a piece of ground where plants are grown.
examples: To work in his garden was one of his most respectable pleasures
I expected at least that the pigs were got into the garden

oewn-03422659-n.learner: a yard or a piece of grass next to a house.
examples: The garden sloping to the road, the house standing in it, the green pales and the laurel hedge, everything declared they were arriving.

oewn-08456800-n.learner: the flowers, vegetables, fruit or herbs that are grown in a garden.
examples: The frost came early and killed half the garden.

oewn-00039019-r.learner: in the way you would expect.
examples: In seeing Bingley, her thoughts naturally flew to her sister
This naturally introduced a panegyric from Jane on his diffidence

oewn-00507808-r.learner: because of what someone or something is in itself.
examples: her feelings; which are naturally lively enough

oewn-00490971-r.learner: in a way that is natural or normal.
examples: She spoke naturally and easily, as if nothing had happened.

oewn-00364717-v.learner: to bring something to an end.
examples: She then hastened away to her mother, who had purposely broken up the card-party
When Lady Catherine and her daughter had played as long as they chose, the tables were broken up

oewn-02752492-v.learner: when an event comes to an end.
examples: When the party broke up, Lydia returned with Mrs. Forster to Meryton
The whist party soon afterwards breaking up, the players gathered round the other table

oewn-00935783-v.learner: to tell people something that only a few people knew, or that was meant to be kept secret.
examples: With the kindest concern he came on to Longbourn, and broke his apprehensions to us in a manner most creditable to his heart.

oewn-01863207-v.learner: to make something come to an end.
examples: Stop me, whilst you can.
she could not use the short pause he allowed in any attempt to stop him farther

oewn-01864781-v.learner: to come to a halt and stop moving.
examples: it was two ladies, stopping in a low phaeton at the garden gate
she was tempted, by the pleasantness of the morning, to stop at the gates and look into the park

oewn-01866904-v.learner: to break off a journey for a while.
examples: On the way north we stopped two nights at my uncle's house.

oewn-01802111-v.learner: to make someone feel pain in the mind.
examples: Do not distress me by the idea.
It is really too distressing, I am sure you must feel it so.

oewn-02609431-v.learner: to bring someone into difficulty or hardship, especially over money.
examples: The failure of the bank distressed many families for years.

oewn-00925764-v.learner: to show a place, a direction, a person or a thing, either in space or in a figure of speech.
examples: She pointed to the house at the end of the lane.

oewn-01154680-v.learner: to turn something so that it is in position to be used.
examples: He pointed the gun at the door and waited.

oewn-00923271-v.learner: to be a sign of something, or a symptom of it.
examples: Every detail of her manner pointed to a settled dislike.

oewn-00034309-r.learner: soon, after only a little time.

oewn-01152997-a.learner: feeling sadness, sorrow or discontent, showing it, or causing it.

oewn-00912446-a.learner: having a general feeling of distress.

oewn-05128718-n.learner: how many units or people a total comes to.
examples: The crowd was larger than expected; the final figure was about three thousand.

oewn-00879379-v.learner: to help someone who is acting or reciting by telling them the next words they have forgotten or half learned.
